claims.claim: JOSS, ReScience, CODECHECK, and ACM artifact policies expose different review objects and warrant different conclusions.
claims.source_locator: JOSS design and review sections; ReScience initiative description; CODECHECK abstract and process; ACM badge definitions
claims.evidence: The sources define repository software review, computational replication reports, independent execution certificates, and differentiated artifact badges respectively.
claims.notes: Claim is deliberately comparative and does not rank effectiveness.

claims.claim: PROV-O, CWLProv, RO-Crate, and Workflow Run RO-Crate provide reusable provenance and research-object semantics but do not themselves decide scientific validity.
claims.evidence: The sources specify representation and packaging of entities, activities, agents, workflows, and run provenance; none claims to adjudicate domain-scientific correctness.
claims.notes: Negative scope statement is limited to what the standards claim to encode.

claims.claim: Claim-centric scholarly representations have substantial prior art in micropublications, nanopublications, and evidence graphs.
claims.evidence: The works explicitly represent claims or assertions with provenance, evidence, argument, or computation.
claims.notes: Used to narrow novelty, not to imply full equivalence.

claims.claim: Global recursive reputation, local trust, and attack-resistant root-relative graph capacity are prior work rather than inventions of this design map.
claims.evidence: EigenTrust defines a global recursive score; Massa and Avesani study local trust; Levien and Aiken define a root-relative flow-based trust metric.
claims.notes: No claim is made that those results transfer directly to scientific review.

claims.claim: The paper proposes a two-layer architecture separating a shared claim/evidence record from plural root-, topic-, capability-, policy-, and time-relative reliance views.
claims.evidence: This is an explicit design choice derived from the evidence packet, not an empirical fact.
claims.notes: Admissible only as proposed design; promotion to recommendation awaits interoperability and comparative evaluation.

claims.claim: Rerenderability, repeatability, reproducibility, independent replication, and scientific validity should not be collapsed into one badge.
claims.source_locator: NASEM terminology discussion; ACM badge categories; manuscript Table 1
claims.evidence: Primary sources support distinguishing repeatability, reproducibility/replicability, availability, functionality, and result reproduction. The exact five-part ladder is the manuscript's normalization.
claims.notes: Manuscript labels the exact arrangement as a design normalization, not universal terminology.

claims.claim: A resource declaration should be multiaxis and include human and agent intelligence as well as compute, storage, access, platform, time, support, cost, and freshness.
claims.evidence: Protocol design judgment motivated by the supplied project requirements and failure analysis.
claims.notes: Requires implementation burden study and independent review.

claims.claim: The two worked cases can be represented without reporting a downselect as equivalent to a full rerun.
claims.evidence: Only narrative design walkthroughs exist in this draft; executable case packets and independent annotation are absent.
claims.notes: Manuscript explicitly calls the cases walkthroughs and marks evidence gates.

claims.claim: Machine checks can establish conformance and discrepancies but not scientific validity.
claims.source_locator: Scope of computational reproduction and independent execution procedures
claims.evidence: Sources distinguish computational checks from broader scientific replication and review; the protocol boundary is a conservative design rule.
claims.notes: Retained as a safety boundary, not a measured finding.

claims.claim: Plural local trust views improve peer-review outcomes relative to global reputation.
claims.source_locator: No scientific-review comparison exists in the supplied packet
claims.evidence: Local trust evidence comes from a recommender setting and cannot establish scientific-review effectiveness.
claims.notes: Excluded from findings and stated only as an open hypothesis.

claims.claim: Polycentric governance is an institutional lens for plural domains, not evidence that plural scientific review works.
claims.source_locator: Ostrom's polycentric-governance framework and manuscript's explicitly limited transfer
claims.evidence: The source establishes multiple decision centers under shared rules; the manuscript explicitly avoids empirical transfer claims.

claims.claim: This design map is the first end-to-end system joining provenance and plural trust governance.
claims.evidence: The primary-source gap audit is incomplete and the supplied closest-work matrix identifies high preemption risk.
claims.notes: Explicitly excluded; do not introduce without a completed novelty audit.
